tipo.cita: We conducted a comparative accuracy study to evaluate and compare the performance of CNN models trained using different image inputs: clinical, dermoscopy, and a combination of clinical and dermoscopy.
This study aimed to adhere to the CLEAR Derm Consensus Guidelines established by the International Skin Imaging Collaboration Artificial Intelligence Working Group.

datos_origen.cita: A total of 914 pairs of images were gathered from public dermatology image repositories, comprising 822 from the “7‐point criteria evaluation database”
and 92 from “The International Skin Imaging Collaboration” 22 (ISIC) repository.
In consideration of our research, which involves the use of images that have been previously published in public repositories

datos_tamano.cita: We divided 914 image pairs into training, validation, and test sets.
Finally, the dataset was divided into 676 pairs of images for training, 119 for validation, and 119 for testing.

datos_pais.buscado: Se leyó el texto completo (líneas 92-851) y se buscó con Python: 'Colombia', 'Spain', 'Argentin', 'Buenos Aires', 'Australia', 'Italy', 'Portugal', 'country', 'hospital', 'patient'. 'Colombia' solo aparece en afiliaciones (líneas 100-153). El texto no dice de qué país son los pacientes o las imágenes; línea 256 dice que las fuentes no dan la ascendencia de los pacientes. La referencia 22, que el texto cita junto a «The International Skin Imaging Collaboration» (líneas 254-255), es «Hospital Italiano de Buenos Aires Skin Lesions» (líneas 799-801), pero el texto no atribuye a ese hospital ni a un país las 92 imágenes.

datos_unidad.cita: Image selection was based on the availability of paired dermoscopy and clinical photographs from the same pigmented skin lesion, diagnosis of melanoma or nevi (any type), and a license/permit for research use.
For the classification algorithm, all lesions were reclassified into binary categories: “1” denoting any type of melanoma and “0” for non‐melanoma lesions (nevi).
a combination of paired clinical and dermoscopy images from the same lesion.

validacion.cita: The diagnoses as reported in the repositories were used for a stratified data splitting into training, validation, and test set.

The training set was employed to train the models, while the validation set was used for initial analysis and to compare model performance metrics across the different hyperparameter sets (further details in the “modeling” section). Subsequently, the test set was employed to compare the performance metrics of the best models, determined by their validation AUC‐ROC scores.

For performance evaluation and comparison on the test set, we selected the best model of each type based on validation AUC‐ROC, and then, we used the De‐Long test to compare correlated ROC curves and the McNemar's test for non‐independent samples to compare sensitivity and specificity.

agrupa_por_paciente.buscado: Se leyó el texto completo (líneas 92-851) y se buscó con Python: 'patient', 'subject', 'group', 'stratif', 'split'. La única descripción de la partición es la estratificación por diagnóstico (línea 258: «The diagnoses as reported in the repositories were used for a stratified data splitting»). 'patient' aparece solo para características demográficas o ascendencia (líneas 256, 258, 642); 'group' solo como «study groups» (línea 262) y «three groups» de modelos (línea 572). No se dice si la partición agrupa por paciente.

metrica_principal.cita: Best models were chosen based on validation AUC‐ROC.
By systematically analyzing metrics such as the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC‐ROC), sensitivity, and specificity

desbalance.cita: Our dataset had predominantly non‐melanoma lesions (class imbalance), which can influence the final models' performance. However, we used a weighted loss function during training to reduce model prediction biases toward non‐malignant lesions.
Training employed Adam for optimization, and loss function weighting adjusted for class imbalance.

resultado_principal.cita: The dermoscopy model displayed the highest AUC‐ROC value of 0.869, followed by the clinical + dermoscopy model at 0.822, and finally, the clinical model at 0.661.
In terms of sensitivity, the clinical + dermoscopy model achieved the highest value at 1.000, followed by the dermoscopy model at 0.799, and the clinical model at 0.513.

Regarding model specificity, the dermoscopy model exhibited the highest value of 0.800, while the clinical model achieved a specificity of 0.650, and the clinical + dermoscopy model registered a specificity of 0.288.

The relatively small sample size, especially within the context of deep learning and big data, was primarily due to the scarcity of paired clinical and dermoscopy images from the same lesion available in public repositories.
